title: SDR sequence copy drafts (PLG signals) — rate-limit pain / spend growth / security intent (A/B variants)
content:
Working draft — SDR copy for PLG→sales “signals” motion. Goal: helpful + specific, avoid creeping people out. We should not claim we “saw your traffic” in a way that feels invasive. Keep it about support + options.

Audience: Eng lead / platform / ML infra (primary); security/procurement when security intent signal.
Tone: engineering-first, short, concrete, opt-out friendly.

----
GLOBAL PERSONALIZATION TOKENS (HubSpot)

Basics
- {{first_name}}
- {{last_name}}
- {{company}}
- {{company_domain}}
- {{title}}
- {{city}} / {{country}}
- {{owner_name}} (SDR)
- {{ae_name}} (AE)

Signal fields (populate from scoring event → HubSpot custom props)
- {{signal_type}} (rate_limit_pain | spend_growth | security_intent)
- {{signal_summary}} (one sentence)
- {{signal_window}} (e.g., “last 14 days”)
- {{metric_1_label}} / {{metric_1_value}} (optional)
- {{metric_2_label}} / {{metric_2_value}} (optional)
- {{models_used}} (optional; be careful)
- {{region}} (optional)
- {{next_best_offer}} (Dedicated capacity | VPC/Private | quota/rate limit tuning)
- {{customer_stage_hint}} (self-serve | evaluated | scaling)

“Safe” phrasing token options (pick one; avoid over-precision)
- {{soft_usage_phrase}} examples:
  - “Some teams hit limits when they start scaling workloads.”
  - “As usage scales, we often see rate limiting become a blocker.”
  - “We’ve seen a few indicators your workload may be outgrowing self-serve settings.”

Compliance / preference
- Always include: “If I’m off, tell me and I’ll close this out.”
- Add opt-out line for email: “Reply ‘no’ and I won’t follow up.”
- Don’t include exact spend ($) or exact 429 counts in first touch. Keep numeric details for live call or if they ask.

Cadence used here: Day 1 / Day 3 / Day 7 / Day 14 (plus LinkedIn touches in between).

----
SEQUENCE 1 — RATE-LIMIT PAIN (repeated 429s / quota friction / burst concurrency)

Trigger notes (internal, not in copy)
- repeated 429s, sustained over 7–14d
- burst concurrency spikes
- repeated model routing failures due to capacity constraints

Primary CTA: 15 min “limits + architecture” chat; offer quick fixes + Dedicated path.

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — A variant (direct/helpful)
Subject options:
1) Quick question on Redwood rate limits
2) Helping teams reduce 429s (Redwood)

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I’m {{owner_name}} at Redwood Inference. Reaching out because {{soft_usage_phrase}} and we often can remove 429s / throttling without big changes.

If you’re open to it, I can share:
- a couple ways teams reduce rate-limits (batching/caching + quota tweaks), and
- when it makes sense to move to Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.

Worth a quick 15 minutes this week? If I’m off-base, reply “no” and I’ll close the loop.

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — B variant (curiosity + “next step”)
Subject options:
1) Are 429s slowing you down?
2) Can I sanity-check your Redwood throughput targets?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Random question — are you running into rate limits or bursty traffic constraints on Redwood right now?

We’ve been helping a few teams move from “works in dev” to “predictable in prod” by tuning request patterns (batching/streaming) and, when needed, setting up Dedicated capacity.

Open to a quick call to compare notes? Happy to keep it tactical.

— {{owner_name}}

LINKEDIN TOUCH 1 (Day 2) — connection request
Note:
Hi {{first_name}} — I work with teams scaling LLM inference on Redwood. If you’re ever dealing with 429s / burst throughput, happy to share what’s worked for others. — {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 2 (Day 3) — “useful artifact”
Subject options:
1) 2 quick ways teams avoid 429s
2) Redwood throughput checklist?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

In case it’s useful, here are two common fixes when teams hit rate limiting as workloads ramp:
1) Enable/adjust batching + caching for the heavy routes (cuts requests/token and smooths bursts)
2) Align quotas/concurrency with peak traffic patterns (so you don’t throttle during predictable spikes)

If you tell me your rough latency target + peak concurrency (ballpark is fine), I can suggest whether you’re a better fit for (a) tuned self-serve settings or (b) Dedicated capacity.

Want to grab 15 min?

— {{owner_name}}

CALL TASK (Day 4/5) — voicemail script (optional)
“Hi {{first_name}}, this is {{owner_name}} at Redwood. Calling because teams at your stage often start seeing 429s/throttling during bursts. We can usually fix it with batching/quota tuning, and if you need predictable peaks we can discuss Dedicated. I’ll send a quick email as well — my number is …”

LINKEDIN TOUCH 2 (Day 6) — short message
“{{first_name}}, if you’re the right person: happy to share a couple concrete knobs for avoiding 429s + improving tail latency. If not, who owns LLM infra/perf at {{company}}?”

EMAIL 3 (Day 7) — “Dedicated angle”
Subject options:
1) Dedicated capacity for predictable peaks?
2) Option if you need guaranteed throughput

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If throttling is tied to bursty peaks (vs. steady growth), the cleanest fix we see is Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs + predictable throughput, with the same Redwood API.

Not sure if that’s relevant for {{company}} — but if you’re aiming for tighter latency SLOs or have launch-driven spikes, I can outline what teams typically reserve and how fast we can stand it up.

Would a 15 min overview be useful?

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 4 (Day 14) — “breakup / permission to close”
Subject options:
1) Close the loop?
2) Should I stop reaching out?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Should I stop reaching out?

If rate limits/throttling aren’t a priority right now, totally fine — I can close this out. If they are, I’m happy to share a quick checklist and bring an SE in for 20 minutes.

— {{owner_name}}

----
SEQUENCE 2 — SPEND / USAGE GROWTH (sustained spend growth, token volume, sustained concurrency)

Trigger notes (internal)
- 14–30d sustained spend growth
- increasing token volume; “staying power” (not a one-day spike)
- repeated “pricing page” visits can be supporting signal (do not cite explicitly)

Primary CTA: planning conversation: cost/latency tradeoffs + commits + Dedicated/Private path.

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — A variant (congrats + cost focus)
Subject options:
1) Scaling Redwood at {{company}}
2) Reducing unit cost as usage grows

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I’m {{owner_name}} at Redwood. Reaching out because it looks like your Redwood usage is scaling, and we usually see teams hit an inflection point where unit cost + predictability matter more than “just getting it working.”

If helpful, we can do a quick planning call on:
- cost-per-1M tokens (what impacts it + how to reduce it)
- caching/batching recommendations for your traffic
- when Dedicated makes sense for steady throughput / lower variability

Open to 20 minutes?

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — B variant (benchmarks + offer)
Subject options:
1) Quick benchmark / cost sanity check?
2) Tradeoffs: latency vs $ as you scale

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

As teams scale LLM inference, the biggest wins are usually operational: batching/caching + the right deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

If you’re open, I can set up a short call and we’ll leave you with:
- 2–3 concrete levers to improve latency/cost for your current workload
- a recommendation on whether Dedicated capacity would pencil out

Is there a 20 min slot this week?

— {{owner_name}}

LINKEDIN TOUCH 1 (Day 2) — message (no metrics)
“Hi {{first_name}} — I work with teams scaling LLM inference on Redwood. Happy to share a quick cost/throughput checklist if useful. If someone else owns inference perf/cost at {{company}}, who should I talk to?”

EMAIL 2 (Day 3) — “commit / pricing guidance” (careful)
Subject options:
1) When a commit starts to make sense
2) Options as usage scales

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

One thing that tends to help once usage is steady: moving from purely on-demand to a small commit (or Dedicated capacity) so spend is more predictable and you can lock in throughput.

No pressure — if you tell me roughly (a) expected growth next quarter and (b) latency SLO, I can point you to the most common setup.

Worth a quick chat?

— {{owner_name}}

CALL TASK (Day 5) — talk track
- Ask: “Are you scaling a single route/model or multiple products?”
- Ask: “What’s your p95 latency target and peak concurrency?”
- Offer: “We can run a lightweight workload review; SE can suggest batching/caching + model profile.”

EMAIL 3 (Day 7) — “Dedicated vs Hosted framing”
Subject options:
1) Hosted vs Dedicated: quick decision tree
2) If predictability is the goal

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

A simple decision tree we use:
- If traffic is spiky/uncertain → Hosted is easiest, but you may see variability
- If traffic is steady/growing and SLOs matter → Dedicated gives predictable throughput + isolation
- If you need residency/SSO/audit controls → Private/VPC may be the right next step

If you tell me which bucket {{company}} is in, I can route you to the right person (or we can keep it self-serve if that’s best).

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 4 (Day 14) — “permission to close”
Subject options:
1) Close this out?
2) Still relevant to chat?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I haven’t heard back — should I close this out for now?

If you *are* planning around higher volumes this quarter, I’m happy to do a quick cost/throughput review and share what Dedicated capacity would look like.

— {{owner_name}}

----
SEQUENCE 3 — SECURITY INTENT (SSO/SAML docs, audit logs, SOC2, residency, security questionnaire)

Trigger notes (internal)
- docs/console engagement on SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2
- “security questionnaire” click / request
- region/residency signals (esp EMEA)

Primary CTA: intro + offer to share security pack / schedule security review w/ SE + security.
Avoid: implying we tracked exactly what pages they viewed.

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — A variant (security pack offer)
Subject options:
1) Security review for Redwood (SOC 2 / SSO / audit logs)
2) Can I send our security packet?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I’m {{owner_name}} at Redwood Inference. I’m reaching out because teams evaluating Redwood for production often need to align on security items (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency).

If you’re at that stage, I can:
- send our current security packet, and
- set up a 25 min call with an SE to walk through requirements + deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC).

Is that useful for {{company}} right now?

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 1 (Day 1) — B variant (procurement timeline)
Subject options:
1) Any security requirements for bringing Redwood to prod?
2) Quick question: security / compliance for inference

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Quick question — are there any security/compliance requirements you need to meet before using Redwood in production (SSO, audit logs, residency, vendor review, etc.)?

If yes, I can connect you with the right folks and share what we support today (and the fastest path depending on your constraints).

Open to a short call?

— {{owner_name}}

LINKEDIN TOUCH 1 (Day 2) — connection request
Note:
“Hi {{first_name}} — I support teams evaluating Redwood for production + security reviews (SSO/audit logs/residency). Happy to connect.”

EMAIL 2 (Day 3) — “residency/Private”
Subject options:
1) Data residency / VPC options
2) Deployment options for security requirements

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If any of your requirements include data isolation or residency, Redwood has options beyond the hosted API:
- Dedicated capacity (isolation + predictable throughput)
- Private/VPC deployments (customer-managed networking, auditability)

If you share your top 2 constraints (e.g., SSO, audit logs, EU-only, on-prem), I’ll suggest the best fit and loop in an SE.

— {{owner_name}}

CALL TASK (Day 5/6) — talk track
- “What’s driving the security review — enterprise customer request, internal policy, regulated data?”
- “Do you need SSO/SAML for Console access? Audit logs? KMS/HSM?”
- “Any hard residency requirements (EU-only / US-only)?”
- Offer: “We can do a 30 min security overview and follow with a doc pack.”

EMAIL 3 (Day 7) — “calendar + next step”
Subject options:
1) Want to loop in our SE for a security overview?
2) Next step: security overview

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If it helps, the usual next step is a 30 min security overview with an SE where we walk through:
- SOC 2 status + security controls
- SSO/SAML + access controls
- audit logs and retention
- deployment modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) based on your constraints

Should I send a couple times?

— {{owner_name}}

EMAIL 4 (Day 14) — “close out”
Subject options:
1) Close out security review thread?
2) Should I stop reaching out?

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Should I close this out?

If security review isn’t on the roadmap right now, all good — tell me and I’ll stop. If it is, I can send our packet and get you scheduled with an SE.

— {{owner_name}}

----
NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS (for internal review)

1) How specific should we be in email #1?
- Sales feedback so far: “Be concrete, but don’t sound like surveillance.”
- Proposal: no exact numbers in first touch; offer to share the levers + ask for their targets.

2) Persona tweaks
- Eng lead: emphasize latency SLOs, reliability, “predictable peaks,” fewer fires.
- Platform/infra: emphasize batching/caching knobs, dedicated pools, routing/fallback.
- Security: emphasize packet, controls, deployment modes, residency.

3) Guardrails
- Do not mention “pricing page visits” or “docs clicks” explicitly.
- Do not mention exact spend.
- Don’t imply we know their end-customer or app.

4) Handoff language to AE/SE
- After reply/interest, SDR should offer SE participation early for rate-limit pain + Dedicated.
- For security intent: SE + (as needed) security team intro.

5) Subject line testing ideas
- Add “throughput” language vs “rate limit” language.
- Avoid “sales-y” keywords.

6) Timing for EMEA
- Lukas asked: avoid US-centric time suggestions; ask for time zone.

Changelog (rough)
- 2025-02-20: added opt-out language + removed numeric spend references.
- 2025-02-24: added security intent sequence + Dedicated/Private framing + LinkedIn copy.
